rows.name: RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH
rows.read_by: `rinzler`, `runtron`, the packaged systemd unit `rinzler@.service`, `bin/fuse_cleanup.py` (`src/system/fuse_helpers.cpp`, `packaging/systemd/rinzler@.service`, `bin/fuse_cleanup.py` and 7 more files)
rows.values: Path of a directory. The text is used as given. An empty value counts as unset. The program creates the directory when it does not exist.
rows.default: Unset: `<repository root>/stats` when the program file path contains `/gen/`. Otherwise `/opt/positron/stats`.
rows.effect: Sets the base directory where the program mounts the FUSE stats. When the instance count is above 1, the program appends `/instance-<id>` to the path. `RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PRESCOPED=1` turns this suffix off.
rows.notes: `--fuse-mount` overrides it and is used as given. `rinzler_proxy` never mounts and ignores it. The packaged unit sets `/var/run/rinzler/<N>` for unit instance N. Its helper `rinzler-descriptor` rejects a path that is not absolute or has fewer than 2 components. Log: `Stats/config mounted at <path>`.

rows.name: RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PRESCOPED
rows.values: Only the exact text `1` has an effect. Every other text is ignored without a message, for example `true`, `yes`, `0` or an empty value.
rows.default: Unset: when the instance count is above 1, the program appends `/instance-<id>` to the FUSE stats mount path.
rows.effect: With `1`, the program mounts the FUSE stats at the base path and adds no `/instance-<id>` suffix. The base path comes from `RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH` or from the built-in default.
rows.notes: No effect with `--fuse-mount`, without `--instance`, or with an instance count of 1. The packaged systemd unit `rinzler@.service` sets `1`. A value in `/etc/rinzler/instance-<N>.env` replaces the value of the unit. With the suffix on, the log holds `FUSE mount point scoped for instance`.

rows.name: RZ_KV_CACHE_GB
rows.values: Whole number of GiB, parsed with `std::stoull`. Text after the leading digits is ignored. Text that does not start with a number aborts rinzler at startup.
rows.default: Unset: the target is half of the hugepage count, in GiB. The default count of 16 hugepages gives 8 GiB. Empty: rinzler aborts at startup.
rows.effect: Sets the target size of the KV cache, for all models together. The value applies only when the arena allocator (`pos_heap_v2`, the default hugepage allocator of the build) is off. With the arena allocator on, rinzler ignores the value and logs a warning.
rows.notes: `--kv-cache-gb` is parsed later and replaces the value. `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR` selects the allocator at run time. Logs: `RZ_KV_CACHE_GB set to <text>`, `Trying to use <N> GB for persistent KV cache`, and with the arena allocator `ignoring static KV cache sizing knob RZ_KV_CACHE_GB`.

rows.name: RZ_RUNFILE_DIR
rows.read_by: `rinzler`, `rinzler_proxy` (`h/rinzler/rinzler-config.hpp`, `src/rinzler.cpp`). The test launcher `t/proxy/rzproxy/launch.py` reads it too.
rows.values: Path of an existing directory that rinzler can write. The text is used as given. An empty value counts as unset. rinzler does not create the directory.
rows.effect: Sets the directory of the run file `rinzler-<pid>.run`. rinzler writes this JSON file after all models have loaded and removes it on a clean shutdown. The file holds the process id, the model names and the instance.
rows.notes: No command-line flag exists. When the directory is not writable, rinzler prints `Error: runfile directory is not writable` and exits with code 1 before it loads a model. Log after the write: `Rinzler ready. Wrote PID file: <path>`.

evidence.quote: spdlog::info("Rinzler ready. Wrote PID file: {}", run_file);

rows.name: RZ_SAVE_TOKENS_PROMPT_ONLY
rows.values: Exactly `0` or `1`. Any other text, including an empty value, stops rinzler at startup with exit code 1.
rows.default: Unset: off. A request with `save_tokens` runs a normal generation. Empty: rinzler exits at startup with code 1.
rows.effect: With `1`, rinzler answers a request that sets `save_tokens` (a request field that returns the rendered prompt and its token ids) before generation. The response holds only the `save_tokens` object, and its `output_tokens` list is empty. Other requests generate as before.
rows.notes: `1` together with `RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS=0` also stops startup. The error log starts with `RZ_SAVE_TOKENS_PROMPT_ONLY validation failed`. With `1`, startup logs `save_tokens requests answer before generation (RZ_SAVE_TOKENS_PROMPT_ONLY=1)`. A value in `/opt/positron/user/config.env` reaches every instance that the packaged systemd unit starts.

rows.name: RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE
rows.values: A date as `YYYY-MM-DD`. The date must be a real calendar date inside the range of the system clock. The year must be 1000 or later. Other text stops startup.
rows.default: Unset: no fixed date. Each request uses the local date of that day. Empty: rinzler logs a validation error and exits with code 1.
rows.effect: Sets one fixed date that rinzler writes into prompts. The Harmony system message (Harmony is the prompt format of gpt-oss models) uses it as the conversation start date. The `strftime_now` function of Hugging Face chat templates uses local noon of that date.
rows.notes: A bad value logs `RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE validation failed`. The `rendered_at` field of a chat `save_tokens` response shows the date. `rinzler_proxy` throws on every generation when its golden file (the recorded token file) declares a `rendered_at` date and the variable does not equal it.

evidence.quote: std::string("RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE must be YYYY-MM-DD, got '") + env + "'");

rows.name: SPDLOG_LEVEL
rows.values: A level name: `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, `critical` or `off`. Case is ignored. The spdlog library parses the text and ignores an unknown name without a message.
rows.default: Unset: the logger keeps the level from `TRON_LOG_LEVEL`. That level is `debug` when `TRON_LOG_LEVEL` is unset.
rows.effect: Changes the level of the TRON logger after `TRON_LOG_LEVEL` is applied. The stderr output and the log file keep the level from `TRON_LOG_LEVEL`. So the variable can hide messages, and it cannot show more messages.
rows.notes: Example: `warn` hides `info` and `debug` lines. `off` stops all log output. Use `TRON_LOG_LEVEL` to get more detail. The form `NAME=LEVEL` sets one logger, and TRON has one logger, `default_logger`. No log line reports the level. The format comes from spdlog v1.17.0.

rows.name: SUDO_USER
rows.read_by: `rinzler`, `runtron`, through libpos startup (`src/system/memory.cpp`). Nothing in TRON sets it. The program `sudo` sets it.
rows.values: Any value, including an empty one. The code tests only that the variable exists.
rows.effect: When the program runs as root and the variable exists, startup stops. The program logs `Please do not run as sudo` and `INIT: Environment setup failed. Aborting.`, and it exits with code 1.
rows.notes: A root process without the variable passes the check, for example a systemd service. A process that is not root is not affected. `rinzler_proxy` does not run this check. The log message gives the reason: a run under `sudo` creates root-owned files in `/dev/hugepages`.

evidence.quote: "Please do not run as sudo as this will create root-owned files in "

rows.name: SYSTEM_CONFIG
rows.read_by: `rinzler`, `runtron`, libpos (`src/pos/driver.cpp`, `src/system/system.cpp`). Also the wrappers `bin/rinzler` and `bin/runtron`, Slice (`bin/slice`), Dice (`bin/dice`) and test launchers.
rows.values: Text of system options, split at white space. Double quotes group a value. Options: `--instance X,Y`, `--devices`, `--app-cores`, `--dev-cores`, `--helper-cores`, `--numa`, `--nr_hugepages`, `--hugepage_file`, `--resource-map`, `--tracer-core`, `--kv-cache-gb`, `--optimize`, `--no-opt`, `--heap-shadow`.
rows.default: Unset: only the system options of the command line apply. With `DICE_DAEMON_CHILD=1`, startup fails when the variable holds no `--instance`.
rows.effect: Gives system options to the program through the environment, for example `--instance X,Y` to select instance X of Y. libpos parses the whole text at startup, after the command line. An option given in both places takes the `SYSTEM_CONFIG` value.
rows.notes: Log: `INIT: environment system config: <text>`. A wrong `--instance` form or device list makes the program log `INIT: invalid SYSTEM_CONFIG` and exit with code 1. Unknown words are ignored without a message. Without `DICE_DAEMON_CHILD=1` this includes `--numa=0`. `bin/rinzler`, `bin/runtron`, Slice and Dice read only `--instance`.

rows.name: TIKTOKEN_ENCODINGS_BASE
rows.read_by: `rinzler`, `rinzler_proxy`, through the `openai-harmony` crate (`rust/harmony/src/lib.rs`, `src/rinzler/harmony.cpp`). `bin/slice` tests for it and sets it for the tests it starts.
rows.values: Path of a directory that holds the file `o200k_base.tiktoken`. The crate checks the SHA-256 hash of the file.
rows.default: Unset: the crate uses a cached copy of the file, or it downloads the file. Empty: the crate looks in the working directory.
rows.effect: The Harmony tokenizer (Harmony is the prompt format of gpt-oss models) reads its vocabulary file from this directory. The crate then uses no download and no shared cache. A missing file or a wrong hash makes the model load fail.
rows.notes: It matters only for a model whose execution name contains `gpt-oss`. The facts come from `openai-harmony` v0.0.8, the version that `rust/harmony/Cargo.toml` pins. The load error text starts with `Failed to load Harmony encoding`. No log line reports the directory in use.

evidence.quote: # $TIKTOKEN_ENCODINGS_BASE instead, with its own hash check and without the
throw harmony_error("Failed to load Harmony encoding '" + name_str +

rows.name: TRACE_FILE
rows.read_by: `rinzler`, `runtron`, through libpos startup (`src/pos/driver.cpp`). The script `perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh` checks the value of a running rinzler.
rows.values: The exact text `traced`, or a file path. The text is not checked at startup.
rows.default: Unset: the destination is `traced`, the Perfetto system daemon. An outside Perfetto client owns the output file. Empty: the first `SIGUSR1` capture aborts the program.
rows.effect: With a file path, a `SIGUSR1` capture is recorded inside the process and written to that file. A `SIGUSR1` capture is a Perfetto trace of 10 seconds that starts when the program receives the signal `SIGUSR1`. Each capture truncates the file.
rows.notes: Startup logs `INIT: perfetto trace destination: <text>`. A path that cannot be opened aborts the program at the first `SIGUSR1`. With `traced` or unset, a non-empty `TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES` aborts the program at `SIGUSR1`. `runtron --trace FILE` records a run to a file without this variable.

rows.name: TRON_AMX_DISABLE
rows.read_by: libtron, inside `rinzler` and `runtron` (`src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp`). Only a build with the CMake option `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` reads it.
rows.values: Only the exact text `1` has an effect. Every other text is ignored without a message, for example `0`, `true` or an empty value.
rows.default: Unset: software attention uses the AMX kernel when the CPU, the operating system and the process permission allow AMX.
rows.effect: With `1`, software attention does not use the AMX kernel (code that uses Intel AMX, a matrix instruction set of the CPU). It uses the AVX-512 code for every KV page. The program reads the value one time, at the first use.
rows.notes: `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` is off by default and on in the `deb` preset. The AMX kernel serves only models with a head size of 128 dimensions and 4 query heads per KV head. The FUSE stats file `/model/<model id>/attention/summary` shows `amx_available`.

evidence.quote: // TRON_AMX_DISPATCH (CMake option, default OFF) adds an opt-in AMX fast path

new_terms.definition: The systemd unit `packaging/systemd/rinzler@.service` that the tron package installs. It starts one rinzler for each instance.
The hugepage allocator `pos_heap_v2`. The build turns it on by default, and `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR` selects it at run time.
A request field of rinzler. When it is true, the response also holds the rendered prompt, its token ids and the output token ids.
The JSON file `rinzler-<pid>.run`. rinzler writes it after all models have loaded and removes it on a clean shutdown.
The prompt format of gpt-oss models. rinzler renders it with the `openai-harmony` crate.
The file of recorded tokens that `rinzler_proxy` replays.
Software attention code that uses Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions), a matrix instruction set of the CPU.
A Perfetto trace of 10 seconds that rinzler or runtron starts when it receives the signal `SIGUSR1`.
The command-line options of rinzler and runtron that select the instance, FPGA cards, CPU cores, NUMA node and hugepages.
The logging library that TRON uses.

notes: All 12 names are environment variables in scope. No row is dropped. Two rows hold facts from third-party source that is not in the checkout. SPDLOG_LEVEL: the checkout only calls spdlog::cfg::load_env_levels and pins spdlog v1.17.0. The level names, the empty-value rule and the rule that only the logger level changes were read in a local copy of spdlog 1.17.0. TIKTOKEN_ENCODINGS_BASE: the checkout pins openai-harmony v0.0.8 (commit ec7606df in rust/harmony/Cargo.lock). The read of the variable, the hash check, the cache fallback and the empty-value behaviour were read in a local copy of that commit. They were not run. Facts left out to keep the word limits. SYSTEM_CONFIG: non-numeric text for --numa, --nr_hugepages, --tracer-core, --kv-cache-gb or inside a CPU list throws inside a noexcept function, and the process terminates without the 'INIT: invalid SYSTEM_CONFIG' line. SYSTEM_CONFIG: each parse outside a Dice grant reloads the resource map, so a --resource-map given only on the command line is replaced by the default search when SYSTEM_CONFIG is set without --resource-map. SYSTEM_CONFIG: the log label and the FUSE stats suffix take --instance from the command line first and from SYSTEM_CONFIG only when the command line has none. SYSTEM_CONFIG: rinzler_proxy and the other builds with the fake FPGA driver never run the full parse; outside a Dice grant they use only --instance. SYSTEM_CONFIG: three test-side parsers (t_rinzler, t_rinzler_proxy, t/proxy/rzproxy/launch.py) do not accept --instance=X,Y, and bin/slice also accepts a bare X,Y. RZ_KV_CACHE_GB: rinzler_proxy reads and stores the value but has no KV cache; the value -1 wraps to the internal 'not set' marker; rinzler_host (fake FPGA driver) never turns the arena allocator on, so the value always applies there. TRACE_FILE: runtron --trace FILE and --trace-gen FILE write the same destination earlier; TRACE_FILE then changes only later SIGUSR1 captures in runtron. Documentation that disagrees with the code. README.md says the system uses the union of the command line and SYSTEM_CONFIG; the resource-map reload above is an exception. The comment in .github/workflows/cpp-coverage.yml says rinzler does not create RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH; ensure_mountpoint creates it. The code comment example 'SPDLOG_LEVEL=debug,console=err' names a logger 'console' that TRON does not create.
